summary: An evidence export can now be asked to destroy the faces in it. Every frame is scanned, and each face found is filled with a solid black box — widened beyond the face and held for the frames either side of it, so a detector that drops a face for a moment does not leave a full-resolution one visible in the middle of a clip nobody will scrub through. It works alongside the existing privacy-zone redaction: a copy can hide the neighbour's window, the faces, or both, and the manifest names each of them separately. The thing the product will not do is overstate it. A privacy zone is a guarantee — a person drew it, it does not move, and the export covers it. Hiding faces is a best effort against an automatic detector that misses faces which are turned away, distant, partly hidden or blurred by motion, and the product says so beside the checkbox before you make the copy, again beside the finished file, and in the bundle's own manifest. It also reports what actually happened: how many frames were scanned, how many detections were destroyed, and how far beyond each face it painted — and it says in plain words that a count of detections is not a count of people. An appliance that cannot do it refuses the export rather than handing back a copy that hid nothing.
compatibility: Additive: exports behave exactly as before unless the new option is ticked, and a bundle that says nothing about faces did not have the pass run on it. Three things to know before relying on it. It reads every frame, so it takes considerably longer than an ordinary export and one export is limited to twenty minutes of footage at a time — the refusal tells you the number. It needs the face-recognition models installed (the same YuNet model the face-recognition feature downloads) and Python with OpenCV on the appliance; without them the export is refused at the moment you ask for it, with a message naming what is missing, rather than producing a bundle that quietly hid nothing. And the result is a re-encoded derivative exactly as a privacy-zone redaction is, so the file will not match the checksums of the original recordings — which stay on the recorder and can be exported separately by somebody entitled to see them. The exported file names itself as redacted. No new permission is needed: hiding faces is strictly more protective than the export an operator could already make. Also fixed while working on this screen: the evidence export dialog had been rendering with no panel behind it since exports shipped — its labels and warnings drew transparently over the page underneath, which was survivable when the dialog was mostly controls and is not once it carries text worth reading.
